topic: Hidden senses beyond the five: proprioception, balance, temperature, pain, interoception
hook: 5 senses nobody taught you in school

slides.title: Proprioception
slides.body: Sensors in your muscles and joints track your limbs. It's why you can touch your nose with your eyes closed.
slides.image_prompt: Wooden artist mannequin balancing gracefully on one leg on a dark tabletop, soft dramatic side light, minimal background

slides.title: Balance
slides.body: Fluid in tiny canals in your inner ear moves as you move. Spin, then stop: it keeps sloshing. That's dizziness.
slides.image_prompt: Three glowing curved glass tubes filled with blue liquid, arranged like inner ear canals, floating in darkness, scientific illustration style

slides.title: Temperature
slides.body: You have separate sensors for cold and heat. Menthol triggers your cold sensors, which is why mint feels cool.
slides.image_prompt: Fresh mint leaves covered in frost crystals on a dark slate surface, cold blue light, macro photography

slides.title: Pain
slides.body: Pain has its own sensors, separate from touch. Your brain tissue has none, so surgeons can operate while you're awake.
slides.image_prompt: Anatomical brain model made of soft pink glass on a dark pedestal, surgical instruments resting beside it, clinical cool lighting

slides.title: Interoception
slides.body: Your sense of inside signals: hunger, thirst, a full bladder, even your own heartbeat.
slides.image_prompt: Glowing red anatomical heart model suspended in darkness, faint pulse rings radiating outward, empty glass of water and bowl nearby

cta: Part 2 tomorrow. Follow, don't miss it
caption:
Sight, hearing, smell, taste, touch. That list leaves out the sense that lets you touch your nose with your eyes closed, and the one that makes mint feel cold.

Depending on how you define a sense, scientists count far more than five. Part 2 drops tomorrow, so follow for one fact your brain won't believe, daily. Save this for the next time someone says 'sixth sense.'

Which of these would you least want to lose?
